Pinch thumb + finger (quick taps — pinch and let go):
• Index finger — L
• Middle finger — Z
• Ring finger — R Right hand C-buttons, A, B and X Camera (C-buttons): move your right palm.

Pinch thumb + finger (quick taps — pinch and let go):
• Index finger — A
• Middle finger — B
• Ring finger — X (not used in most games) Start and menu Pinky tap and hold Quick tap right thumb + little finger — Start.

Hold the same pinch for about 1 second — VR menu.

In the menu: move your left palm to move the highlight, tap right index finger to pick. The menu pointer stays controller-only in v1.

Tip: if the menu keeps opening instead of Start, snap the pinky pinch faster — like snapping your fingers. Tips Controllers, light and tracking • Your hands are the controller — no controller needed.
• Pick up a controller any time and it takes over from that hand instantly. Put it down and the hand takes over again.
• Hand tracking needs light — a dim room makes it worse.
• If a hand leaves the headset view, its buttons release — nothing gets stuck.
• Close this guide with the B button (right middle-finger pinch). AR mode Your room, with the game on a floating screen On — games open in your room Off — games open in VR Placing the screen Move it and resize it with your hands Turn AR mode on, then start a game — the game opens on a floating screen in your room, with your room visible around it.

To move the screen: hold the right pinky pinch for about 1 second to open the VR menu, move the highlight to Adjust screen, and tap right index finger to pick it. Then hold a grip — left middle-finger pinch, or a right fist — and move your hand: the screen follows it. Move your palm up or down to resize it. Tap A or B (right index or middle pinch) when it is where you want it.

To put it back in front of you: VR menu, Reset screen.

The screen position is saved, so next time it opens where you left it. AR tips Light, tracking and switching back • AR mode is the passthrough toggle: the game floats in your room instead of filling the view.
• Hand tracking needs light — a dim room makes it worse.
• To switch back to VR: hold the right pinky pinch to open the VR menu, move the highlight to Passthrough, and tap right index finger. The game returns to the big VR screen.
• Games that use immersive fullscreen open as a floating screen while AR mode is on.
• Your room stays private: the headset shows it to you only — nothing is recorded or sent anywhere. Digital controller A 3D N64 controller you can pick up Hand mode Hand gestures Digital controller Placing the controller Pick it up and put it where you play The digital controller is the 3D N64 controller floating in your room. Pick it up and hold it while you play: it follows your hand, and the game feels your fingers pressing its buttons — thumb on the stick, fingers on A, B, Start, the C-buttons, L, R, Z and the D-pad. Its buttons glow and its stick tilts as you play, so you can see what you are pressing.

To pick it up: reach for it and hold a grip — left middle-finger pinch, or a right fist. It attaches to your hand. Open your hand to put it down where you are playing; the spot is saved, so next time it is there.

While you are holding it, that grip is the hold, not a game button: your Z and D-pad modifier come from pressing the controller's own Z and D-pad instead. The hand that is not holding it keeps working the same way — its fingers press the controller's buttons too. Let go of the controller and you are back to the main hand-gesture mode: left palm is the stick, pinches are the buttons.

To move it to a new home spot: hold the right pinky pinch for about 1 second to open the VR menu, move the highlight to Place controller, and tap right index finger to pick it. Then hold a grip and move your hand: the controller follows it. Let go to put it down. Tap A or B (right index or middle pinch) when it is where you want it. Controller tips Modes, hands and switching back • There are two hand-tracking modes, and the main one is never removed: Hand gestures (left palm is the stick, pinches are the buttons) is the default, and Digital controller is the one you hold.
• Switching is one tap: in the VR menu, Hand mode flips straight between them; in the library, the Digital controller section's Hand mode tile does the same. No cycling through the screen and off display modes.
• The Controller row in the VR menu still cycles the four display modes (3D in hands, 2D below screen, the placed 3D controller, Off) for when you want those.
• To hold it, grip close to it: a grip only picks it up when your hand is right next to it, so a Z pinch or D-pad fist made anywhere else stays a game button.
• Either hand can pick it up, and one hand is enough to play.
• Hand tracking needs light — a dim room makes it worse. High values can reveal missing geometry at the edges. Both eyes (double pass) 3D (experimental) On: each eye gets its own view. Starts with the GLideN64 video plug-in. Tap for immersive. Off. Tap to give this game depth in the headset. Tuning a single eye, set in the game’s settings. Tap to switch off. Immersive Immersive resolution per eye Immersive world size Shows the scene at a smaller angle, as if the game's camera had a narrower view. Head turns still match. Below 100% the picture no longer fills the whole view. Sharper small textures Upscales small textures with xBRZ, for HUD fonts that fall apart when spread over the whole view. Costs memory and some speed, and changes the look. Immersive HUD size How wide the HUD is spread. At 100% it spans as much of your view as the game's own camera, which can push it into the corners of your eye. Immersive camera distance Moves the camera back, for games whose camera sits very close, like racing games. 100% doubles the distance to the nearest object. Things right behind the old camera may be missing. Instead of a screen, the game fills your view and turning your head turns the camera. Parts of the world the game did not expect to be seen may be missing at the sides. Immersive: the game fills your view and follows your head. Tap to switch off. Depth boost Spreads a deep scene in depth, for racing games whose track otherwise sits almost at the horizon. 0% is physically correct.
